newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks need consensus to lower inflation - IMF/Hardy.
newsitem.headline: Turks need consensus to lower inflation - IMF/Hardy.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund (IMF) figure has said that Turkey needed political consensus to lower chronic inflation and urged the government to implement an anti-inflation programme.

"Turkey faces chronic inflation for many years but has been unable to create a political consensus to solve this serious problem," Martin Hardy, the IMF Assistant Director to Europe, told a Euromoney conference in Istanbul which ended on Thursday.
Hardy, who also heads the IMF Turkey desk, said although high inflation was something that Turks had become accustomed to, it had a serious and negative impact on the economy.

"Inflation is a kind of tax that deteriorates income distribution as you take from poor and give it to rich people. This reverse income distribution raises social problems in the country," Hardy said.
"Our advice to the government is to detail its medium-term programme to tackle chronic inflation. They must work with coordination and insist on realising this target," he said.
Turkey's annual consumer inflation stood at 77.2 percent in April, compared with 77.3 percent in the same period in 1996.
Hardy said Turkey had showed some economic improvement in recent years, with higher growth, but saw weakness in public finances as one of the country's major problems.
"Turkey grew very fast in recent years, but that must not be seen as a good performance as the country faced economic and political crises, causing a volatility in the financial markets," Hardy said.
"Turkey has potential but cannot use it. The government should maintain coordination between financial and monetary policies, and as the IMF, we are ready to help," he said.
